model_output.verdict: A computer science graduate with a relevant internship, but the internship bullets leave too much to guess.
write_up: You’re aiming for software engineering, with a React and Spring Boot internship and several working projects. A recruiter can follow that path, but the internship doesn’t name the features you developed or show the size or results of the work. They’re likely to hesitate and move on unless the pile is thin.

The finance tracker line is a good model: it names the application, what it does, and the tools used. Put Experience above Education, and give the inventory application the same treatment. The May 2026 degree helps account for time after the internship.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: The job target is clear, but the rest could belong to almost any graduate. Use this space to point to work you've actually done.

cards.line: Education sits above Experience.

cards.line: - Responsible for developing features for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are named, but the features aren't. A recruiter has to guess what you actually developed.

cards.question: Which features did you develop for the inventory application?

cards.line: - Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meetings tell a recruiter how the team worked, not what you contributed. There's room here for a decision or task you took on.

cards.question: What task or decision did you contribute during sprint planning or stand-ups?

cards.line: - Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: The tests could cover almost anything. Name what you tested and the tool you used; include a verified result if you have one.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [features or components] using [test tool], [result if known]
cards.question: What did you test, which tool did you use, and what changed if you know?

cards.line: - Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The people, requirements, and solutions are all unnamed. One concrete example would show what your part in the collaboration was.
cards.example: Collaborated with [teams] to gather requirements for [feature or problem] and deliver [solution]
cards.question: Which teams did you work with, and what requirement and solution did you contribute to?

cards.line: - Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what kind of bugs you fixed or what you reviewed. Pick an example that shows the work.
cards.example: Fixed [specific bug] and performed code reviews for [code or feature]
cards.question: What bug did you fix, and what code or feature did you review?

cards.line: - Provided technical support to students and faculty for hardware and software issues
cards.cannot_tell: Students, faculty, hardware, and software give the setting, but not the problems you handled. A specific issue would make the support work more concrete.
cards.example: Provided technical support to students and faculty for [specific hardware or software issues]
cards.question: What hardware or software issues did you regularly help students and faculty solve?

cards.line: - Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The ticket volume and types of solutions aren't named. Those details would show what the help desk work involved.
cards.example: Resolved [number] tickets [time period] involving [issues] and documented solutions in [location or format]
cards.question: How many tickets did you resolve, what did they concern, and where did you document solutions?

cards.line: - Built a Python application to track expenses and visualize spending with matplotlib
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It names what you built, what it does, and the tools without making a recruiter guess.

fit.note: Your internship and projects point toward entry-level software engineering work. The inventory application needs more detail about your individual contributions.
